info.title: TheSignup API
info.description: Public REST API for TheSignup. Agent-friendly: every endpoint is OpenAPI-described, Bearer-authenticated via long-lived API keys, rate-limited per credential, and idempotency-keyed for safe retries. Errors follow RFC 7807 problem details with stable `code` enums.

ApiKey.description: Long-lived org-scoped API key. Generate one from your account dashboard. Pass as `Authorization: Bearer sgn_live_…`.

cause.description: Extension member used by upgrade_required to surface the structured upgrade target (kind, currentTier, requiredTier, featureLabel). `featureLabel` is a stable English phrase naming the gated capability (e.g. "host more active events"); it is never translated, so clients may compare it.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 7807 problem details. All API errors follow this shape; agents should switch on the `code` field.

allOf.description: The user behind the credential. Today every organization is 1:1 with a personal user; multi-user orgs will return null when the credential isn't tied to a specific human.

scopes.description: Scopes granted to this credential. Empty array = full owner-equivalent (the default until the OAuth scope model lights up).

placeholder.description: Example answer, shown as a hint in the answer box. Absent when none was given.

maxPerPerson.description: The most spots one person may take on this slot. 1 (the default) is one spot per person; 0 is no per-person limit.

customField.description: The slot's own question, as stored. Read `question` for what the slot actually asks — a slot generated from a repeating shift may inherit the shift's question when this is null.

allOf.description: The question participants are asked when taking this slot: the slot's own, else the repeating shift's. Null when nothing is asked.

questionSource.description: "own" when `question` is the slot's own; "series" when inherited from its repeating shift; null when nothing is asked.

name.description: The question text. Trimmed, then 1 to 200 characters, when sent to the slot update door.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone override for this batch. When set, naive `startTime` / `endTime` strings parse as wall-clock time in that zone. Falls back to the parent signup's `timezone` when absent.

message.description: Participant-facing: prepended to the email, and the text when they consented, each person who held an Open claim on the item is sent when `release_claims` is true. Not a private note. Ignored when nobody is told.

deleted.description: Always `true`: the item and its claims are gone.

claims.description: Units that had been claimed, summed across the claims that were deleted. 0 when the item had no claims.

claimants.description: People who held a claim — a party of three is one claimant. 0 when the item had no claims.

notified.description: Who was told: distinct claimants, emails sent, texts sent. Only holders of an Open claim are told; claims that were Locked (past or cancelled date) are deleted without a message. All 0 when the item had no claims.

date.description: The calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the signup's timezone.

seriesId.description: The Slot Series that generated this day, or null for a day added by hand or an ordinary signup's day.

cancelledAt.description: When the day was called off, or null. A cancelled day keeps its slots, items and registrations. A repeating schedule's date is cancelled through its Shifts instead and keeps null here; read `noLiveTime`.

noLiveTime.description: True when the day had times and none of them is live any more — participants are not offered it, exactly as a cancelled day.

allOf.description: The Day Question asked once per day of whoever signs up for anything that day: the day's own, else the repeating schedule's default. Null when none.

questionSource.description: Whose `question` it is: the day's own, or the schedule's default it inherits. Null when there is no question.

created.description: False when the date was already there and the existing day came back.

seededShifts.description: Shifts the repeating schedule's plan put on a newly created date. 0 on a reused date.

seededItems.description: Items every other date already carries, copied onto a newly created date. 0 on a reused date.

unseededReason.description: Why a new date on a repeating schedule got no Shifts: `out-of-range` (outside the schedule's range — extending the schedule will not fill it; add Shifts with POST /signups/{id}/slot_series/{seriesId}/occurrences after extending) or `empty-rule`. Null otherwise.

location.description: Repeating schedules only: the place for every live Shift on this date, shown to participants. `""` or `null` clears it back to the schedule's default, then the signup's. Participants are told when the place they go to changes.

message.description: Sent with `location` only: added to the email and text participants receive about the new place. Up to 2000 characters.

updated.description: Live Shifts on the date that took the place.

previousPlace.description: Where participants were told to go before.

place.description: Where they go now, after the schedule's and signup's fallbacks.

notified.description: Who was told. Zero when the place participants go to did not change.

placeChange.description: Present only when the request sent a `location`.

days.description: Live days written. Cancelled days are skipped.

signupCloseDate.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Null = signups never close until the event.

maxParticipants.description: Cap on total participants. Null only on a plan with no participant ceiling (uncapped); elsewhere the cap is stored as the plan ceiling.

commitmentRequired.description: When true, a participant must claim a slot or an item to sign up — attending without committing to anything is not offered.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the organizer attached to this signup. Display surfaces should prefer this over the viewer's local zone when rendering eventDate / slot times.

eventWideCustomField.description: Optional one-off field shown on every signup form.

days.description: Every day of the signup in date order, cancelled ones included. Same shape as `GET /signups/{id}/days`.

nextCursor.description: Pass to the next call to fetch the following page. Null when no more pages.

eventDate.description: ISO-8601 datetime. Either UTC (`...Z`) / offset-bearing, OR a naive local string (`2026-09-15T17:00`) — naive form requires `timezone` to also be set; the server then interprets the string as wall-clock time in that zone.

signupCloseDate.description: ISO-8601 datetime, same rules as eventDate. Defaults to never (signups stay open until the event).

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`). When provided, naive `eventDate`/`signupCloseDate`/slot times are parsed against this zone, and the value is stored on the signup so display surfaces can render the organizer's wall-clock intent.

title.description: Cannot be null: a signup always has a title.

eventDate.description: ISO-8601 datetime, same rules as on create: UTC / offset-bearing, or a naive local string that is read in `timezone` (this request's, else the signup's stored one). Refused with 400 on a recurring (Series) signup unless it is the signup's current date: a recurring signup's dates come from its schedule. A multi-day signup built from days alone is not locked. A naive string is read in the signup's stored zone when `timezone` is omitted; it is refused (422) if `timezone: null` is sent beside it.

signupCloseDate.description: ISO-8601 datetime, same rules as `eventDate`. Null = signups stay open until the event.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name. Changing it does NOT move the signup's stored instants (`eventDate`, slot times): it changes how they are displayed and how naive datetimes are read. Null is a no-op (a signup always has a timezone), not a way to clear it.

maxParticipants.description: Cap on total participants. Above the plan's ceiling is refused with 402 `upgrade_required`. Null resets the cap to the plan's ceiling (e.g. 50 on Free), it does NOT remove the cap; only a plan with no ceiling stores null (uncapped). Omit to leave the cap alone.

isPrivate.description: May be changed on a published signup; takes effect immediately.

eventWideCustomField.description: Null removes the one-off field from the signup form.

message.description: Participant-facing: the organizer's note, included in the cancellation EMAIL sent to every attending registration, and in the cancellation TEXT for those with an account who have texts on, a phone, and SMS consent. Omit it to send the standard cancellation notice with no note. Never private; do not put anything here you would not tell the participants.
message.example: The park is closed for repairs. We will reschedule.

recipients.description: The audience: distinct registrations attending when the signup was cancelled, including people who opted out of the email. Not a send count; `emails` and `sms` are.

emails.description: Cancellation emails the mail transport accepted.

signupCloseDate.description: The new close date, a moment in the future (a past or present one is refused with 400 and nothing is written). ISO-8601, same rules as PATCH: UTC / offset-bearing, or a naive local string read in the signup's stored timezone. Always sets the signup's `signupCloseDate`, replacing the old one.

seriesDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, the Series key — not the calendar date of `startTime`.

capacity.description: 0 means uncapped — there is no number to be at or below.

isPast.description: The Occurrence's DATE is behind today in the signup's timezone. Derived per request, server-side, so every surface agrees about the same date.

signupId.description: The participant's registration id — the handle to address them by, without an address being on this payload.

occurrencesTaken.description: Distinct Occurrences of THIS Shift they hold. Per Shift, never per signup.

topItemName.description: Their most frequent Item on this Shift's Occurrences. Null if they bring none.

occurrenceCount.description: Occurrences of this Shift, cancelled ones included.

shiftIndex.description: Position in the Series' shift plan. `(seriesId, shiftIndex)` IS the Shift.

startTime.description: ISO-8601 UTC, taken from the Shift's next upcoming Occurrence — or its last one once the Shift is over.

averageFill.description: Mean `filled` across every non-cancelled Occurrence, PAST INCLUDED, to one decimal. Null when the Shift has no non-cancelled Occurrence at all — no data is not a measurement of zero.

cells.description: Every Occurrence, past and cancelled included, ordered by `seriesDate`.

regulars.description: Top four participants by Occurrences of this Shift taken, ties broken by name. Names and counts only — no email addresses; see the endpoint description.

uncapped.description: Upcoming Occurrences with no capacity to be at or below. On the payload so `staffed + short + uncapped` closes over the upcoming Occurrences.

shortDates.description: The `seriesDate`s behind `short`, so a caller never re-derives the predicate.

itemsUnclaimed.description: Items scoped to an upcoming Occurrence with units still needed.

scope.description: WHO to message, resolved server-side against the signup's roster. `all` everyone attending; `day` one date; `shift` one Occurrence of a repeating slot; `person` one participant; `roster` everyone who has ever held one repeating Shift, across every date it runs; `gaps` the same people, worded as an ask to cover a short date.

scopeId.description: What the scope names, when it names something: an `event_days` row id for `day`, a `time_slots` row id (one Occurrence) for `shift`, a participant registration id for `person`, `<seriesId>#<shiftIndex>` for `roster` and `gaps` (read both off `slot_coverage`). Omitted for `all`, which names itself.

selections.description: Slots/items the participant is signing up for. Empty for headcount-only events. A selection whose slot or item asks a Required question must carry a non-blank `customFieldResponse`, or the request is refused with 400 naming the question.

dayCustomFieldResponses.description: Answers to Day Questions, keyed by event day id. A Required Day Question must be answered for every day the registration touches (a slot on it, an item scoped to it, or day attendance) or the request is refused with 400 naming the question. On a repeat registration the map is merged by key over what is already held; a blank value clears that day's answer.

attendDayIds.description: Event day ids the participant is attending, beyond the days implied by their slots. Written with the registration; a day of another signup, a cancelled day, or a day on a commitment-required signup is refused with 400.

confirmationToken.description: Returned to the participant so they can later edit/cancel their registration without re-authenticating. Show it in the success page; agents should preserve it. Present for a new registration, and for a repeat registration only when the caller's credential belongs to the organization that owns the signup. Otherwise — an anonymous or foreign-org repeat for an email already registered — the response carries no token and `success: false`, nothing is changed, and the manage link is emailed to the address on file.

attendees.description: How many people this registration covers, the person included.

nameVisible.description: Whether the person's name is shown on the public signup page's list of who signed up.

days.description: The event days (`event_days.id`) this person is attending, sorted by id. Includes the day a slot they hold is on, unless it was removed with `days`.

name.description: The person's name as the organizer sees it, and as the public list shows it when `nameVisible`.

email.description: The person's address. Written directly, as the dashboard's edit does: no confirmation email goes to either address. Another registration on this signup already using it is a 409.

phone.description: The person's phone, or null to clear it. A number different from the one on file turns their SMS consent off: they are not texted until they opt in again.

attendees.description: How many people this registration covers, the person included. At most the signup's `maxAttendeesPerSignup` (400 otherwise), and within the signup's capacity.

nameVisible.description: Whether the person's name is shown on the public signup page's list of who signed up.

days.description: The event days (`event_days.id`, from the signup's `days`, as get_signup returns them) this person attends, as the COMPLETE list. Because `days` REPLACES the whole set, read the current list first (the registration's `days`, returned by every registration read and write) and send it back with your change: a day you omit is REMOVED. Removing attendance is allowed on any day, past or cancelled, and `[]` removes all of it; their slots and items stay. Safe to repeat. Adding a day follows the Guest's rules: the signup must be accepting signups, a cancelled date is refused, a required day question must already be answered, and on a signup that requires a commitment no day can be added (so attendance removed there cannot be re-added through `days`). Also refused: adding a day that has passed (400), and adding any day while the registration is no longer attending (400; `[]` still works). A day of another signup is 404. Any refusal writes nothing. Notifies nobody.

toSlotId.description: The slot to move this Commitment to, on the same signup. The person's place moves with its id unchanged; the slot's day is added to the days they attend.

sent.description: The confirmation email was handed to the mail provider.

ratio.description: registered ÷ capacity, capped at 1. Null when capacity is 0.

shortBy.description: Headcount or item-quantity short of full coverage.

capacity.description: Event-wide max participants. Null when uncapped.

gaps.description: Slots and items still short of capacity. Empty when full.

averageHoursBetweenRegistrations.description: Average inter-arrival time across the registration window. Null when fewer than 2 registrations.

tier.description: The tier the org is *entitled to right now* — what rate limits and feature gating will actually enforce. Not necessarily the plan last paid for: a canceled subscription reports the paid tier until its period ends and `free` after, and a support grant reports the granted tier. Build against this value.

suggestedDate.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) if a date was named or implied; otherwise null. For multi-day events, the first day.

endDate.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last day of a multi-day event (inclusive); null for single-day events.

startTime.description: The event's own wall-clock start, 24-hour HH:MM, for events without per-slot shifts. Null or omitted when the times live on timeSlots or none was given.

endTime.description: The event's own wall-clock end, 24-hour HH:MM, paired with startTime. Null or omitted when unknown or when the event uses timeSlots.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles") when it could be inferred; otherwise null.

paused.description: `true` pauses the endpoint; `false` resumes it and clears the paused reason.

pausedReason.description: Free-form note surfaced in the dashboard's paused-reason banner. Requires `paused`; ignored when `paused: false`.

endpointId.description: Required. Scopes the replay to one endpoint, so a filter-driven request can never fan out across every endpoint the org owns.

deliveryIds.description: Explicit selection, 1–500 ids. An empty array is rejected rather than read as "none".

BulkReplayRequest.description: Provide either `deliveryIds` or a non-empty `filter`. Supplying neither is rejected with 422: an unbounded request would re-deliver every row for the endpoint, which is not a designed action.

replayedCount.description: How many deliveries were re-enqueued. Zero when nothing matched.

AuditDiff.description: Field-level before/after pairs. Present on update / publish / cancel; omitted on bare create / delete actions where the row itself is the diff.

credentialId.description: API-key id or OAuth access-token id, depending on `credentialMethod`. `null` for dashboard actions.

credentialLabel.description: Human-readable credential name at the time of the action (snapshot — rotating or revoking the credential does not alter past audit entries).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; `null` when this is the last page. Pass back verbatim as `?cursor=`.

isFirstParty.description: True for clients TheSignup operates itself; these skip the consent screen.

connectedByUserId.description: The user who granted consent. Not expanded — join against your own records if you need a display name.

patch.description: Partial update — supplied fields only. Use null to clear nullable fields. The slot must belong to the signup in the path (a slot of another signup is `404 not_found`, and nothing is written). `customField` is the slot's own question (null removes it, so a date of a repeating schedule asks the schedule's question again). `maxParticipants` below the number of spots already taken is refused with `400`. A date of a repeating schedule (its `seriesId` is set) cannot have its `startTime` edited onto another day of the signup's timezone: that is `409 conflict` and nothing is written — move it with `POST /signups/{id}/slots/{slotId}/move` instead. A time edit that keeps the start on the same local day (including any `endTime` change) is allowed, as is any edit of a slot that is not part of a schedule.

delete.description: Delete an empty one-off slot, immediately. The slot must belong to the signup in the path (a slot of another signup is `404 not_found`, and nothing is written). A date of a repeating schedule (its `seriesId` is set) is refused with `409 conflict`: cancel it instead with `POST /signups/{id}/slots/{slotId}/cancel`. A slot with registrations is also `409 conflict` — on a past date too — and nothing is deleted; remove the registrations first. So is a slot with an item scoped to it that has claims: deleting the slot would move those claims to the whole signup without telling anyone (and unlock them on a past date), so delete those items first (`DELETE /signups/{id}/items/{itemId}?release_claims=true`) or re-scope them (`PATCH /signups/{id}/items/{itemId}`). Items scoped to the slot that nobody has claimed are kept and become whole-signup items (`scope: null`) when the slot goes. Deleting by id is idempotent in effect: a second DELETE of the same slot is `404 not_found`. Notifies nobody.

get.summary: List the OAuth clients connected to the calling org
get.description: One entry per (client, user) connection, org-wide. Not paginated — a single org's connected-agent list is bounded by how many clients its members have authorized. Requires `audit_log:read`: the same compliance-facing scope as the audit log, since this answers 'who has access to our data'.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Per-minute request budget for this credential's tier

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current per-minute window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the per-minute window resets

401.description: Unauthenticated — credentials missing, malformed, invalid, or revoked

403.description: Forbidden — credentials valid but lack the required scope

429.description: Rate limited or daily ceiling exceeded
